rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 6 compounds if possible and map the full elution window without risking truncation. This gives a useful first picture of retention spread and any severe co-elutions before narrowing the window or adjusting slope.

All pairs are fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to reduce t_last. Keep the same broad window and temperature but shorten the gradient to compress the run while checking whether the current worst pair still stays above 1.5.

Resolution is still far above the 1.5 threshold for every pair, so continue shortening the gradient at the same selectivity settings to push t_last below 10 min. This directly targets the remaining time penalty while staying conservative because the worst pair still has a large margin.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so now test whether an even faster method still preserves full resolution and t_last under 10 min. If it does, this will identify a shorter equally optimal method and define how much margin remains before resolution or time starts to fail.

Resolution still has a large safety margin, so continue reducing tG to find the shortest method that remains fully resolved. This efficiently brackets the minimum usable gradient time while keeping all other factors fixed.

The worst-pair resolution remains comfortably above 1.5, so shorten the gradient again to approach the true minimum analysis time. This continues the one-variable search for the shortest fully resolved method before exploring narrower windows or higher temperature.

At tG 6 min the limiting pair is still well resolved (R 2.46), so one more step shorter should reveal whether we can push to the practical minimum gradient time without losing CRF. This is the fastest way to locate the edge of failure on gradient steepness.

The worst pair is only slightly above the 1.5 threshold at tG 4 min, so testing the minimum allowed tG will show whether resolution finally breaks and will bracket the shortest robust method. If it fails, the current tG 4 method is essentially optimal on speed at this window and temperature.

We have bracketed the speed limit at 40 C: tG 4 works and tG 2 fails because pair 1/2 collapses. Raise temperature one step while keeping tG 4 to see whether selectivity changes can either preserve or improve the critical early-pair margin, which could open a path to a still faster method.

At tG 4 the critical pair worsened when temperature increased, so test one step lower to see if selectivity for that pair improves. This probes whether temperature can make the 4 min method more robust while keeping the run very short.

Lowering temperature improved the limiting 1/2 pair at tG 4, so now retest the minimum tG at 35 C to see whether that selectivity gain is enough to make the 2 min gradient fully resolved. This is the most direct route to a shorter equally optimal method.

The critical pair improves as temperature decreases, but tG 2 is still not enough at 35 C, so check 30 C at tG 4 to see whether we can gain more selectivity margin. If the trend continues, that will confirm low temperature as the robust fast operating point and help judge whether 2 min is still unrealistic.

The 1/2 pair continues to improve as temperature drops, so test the shortest gradient again at 30 C. This determines whether the selectivity gain is finally enough to make tG 2 viable, or confirms that 4 min is the true minimum regardless of temperature.

Temperature reduction consistently helps the limiting first pair, so test the lowest allowed temperature at tG 4 to maximize resolution margin at the shortest fully successful gradient found so far. This also tells us whether 25 C is the most robust fast method before deciding if more phi-window optimization is worth pursuing.

The limiting pair has improved steadily as temperature decreases, so one final test at the minimum tG and minimum T will establish whether 2 min can ever reach full resolution. If it still fails, tG 4 is conclusively the shortest viable gradient and we can stop chasing further speed by tG alone.

tG 2 is conclusively too steep, so keep the successful 4 min, 25 C conditions and now narrow the gradient window from the high-organic end. The last peak is out by 4.47 min, so a lower phi1 may still elute everything while reducing gradient steepness and potentially improving the critical 1/2 pair.

Lowering phi1 at tG 4 substantially improved the critical pair, suggesting the narrower window gives better useful selectivity. Retest tG 2 with this narrower window to see whether it can now cross the full-resolution threshold and become a shorter optimal method.

At phi1 0.80 and tG 2 the limiting pair is just below the 1.5 cutoff, so make the gradient slightly shallower by lowering phi1 one step while keeping the same short tG and low temperature. This is the most targeted way to try to lift the 1/2 pair over the threshold without giving up the very fast 2 min program.

We have now achieved full resolution with the 2 min gradient by narrowing phi1 to 0.75, so probe one more step lower in phi1 to see whether the fast method can remain fully resolved with even more margin on the critical pair. This tests the lower edge of the useful window while keeping the shortest successful tG.

The 2 min method remains fully resolved and the critical pair keeps improving as phi1 is lowered, so test one more step down to map the lower limit before the late compound is pushed too far into the hold. This defines how much window narrowing is possible while preserving the shortest successful gradient.

Phi1 0.65 still gives full resolution and keeps the last peak under 10 min, so step down once more to locate the lowest high-organic endpoint that still preserves a maximal CRF. This should identify the edge where the last compound begins to linger too long in the hold.

We have bracketed phi1, with 0.65–0.75 all giving CRF 1.000 and 0.60 too low because the last peak is delayed; now raise phi0 one step to reduce time spent at very weak solvent while keeping the successful short-window shape. This may speed the late compound without sacrificing the now-adequate resolution of the first pair.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 preserved full resolution and slightly reduced t_last, so take one more step higher to see whether the earliest pair and overall run can be compressed further without dropping below the 1.5 threshold. This refines the fastest fully resolved 2 min window from the low-organic side.

The critical pair keeps improving as phi0 increases, while t_last remains essentially unchanged, so move phi0 up one more step to tighten the low-end window further. This tests whether we can keep full resolution with an even more concentrated and still very fast 2 min gradient.

With one injection left, continue the successful trend: increasing phi0 has steadily improved the limiting pair while keeping all 6 peaks observed and t_last low. This final step checks the tightest low-end window likely to remain fully resolved, potentially giving the most robust shortest method among the 2 min gradients.
